uncited: Reflective Gaussian Splatting (Ref-Gaussian) is a framework for the real-time, high-quality rendering of reflective objects with inter-reflection effects, addressing the limitations of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting in modeling complex surfaces and multi-view inconsistencies.

It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [3D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](2812-3d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md) by utilizing 2D Gaussian primitives for view-consistent geometry and employing physically based deferred rendering with split-sum approximation to stabilize optimization and enable efficient inter-reflection modeling without heavy Monte Carlo sampling.
Ref-Gaussian extends the Gaussian splatting framework by replacing 3D ellipsoids with 2D oriented planar Gaussian disks and applying deferred shading on pixel-level feature maps.

- **Multi-view inconsistencies**: Standard 3D Gaussians struggle with detailed geometry due to multi-view inconsistencies.
- **Optimization stability**: Shading directly on Gaussians before alpha-blending can lead to noise in geometry and material.
- **Visibility accuracy**: Using Monte Carlo sampling across Gaussians for visibility can be slow and noisy.
- **Time Complexity**: Real-time rendering is achieved by using the split-sum approximation to avoid heavy Monte Carlo sampling and by using efficient rasterization of 2D Gaussians.
- **Memory Complexity**: Requires storage for 2D Gaussian primitives and pixel-level feature maps.
The extracted mesh for visibility computation also adds memory overhead.
- **Strengths**: High-quality rendering of reflective objects, accurate inter-reflection modeling, stable optimization, real-time performance.

- **Limitations**: Requires an extracted mesh for visibility computation, which may add complexity to the pipeline. 2D Gaussians may have limitations in representing complex 3D structures compared to 3D Gaussians in some scenarios.
- **When to use**: When rendering reflective objects with complex inter-reflection effects is required, and real-time performance is necessary.
- **When not to use**: When the scene does not have significant reflective properties or inter-reflection effects, standard 3D Gaussian Splatting may be sufficient and simpler.
Reflective Gaussian Splatting (Ref-Gaussian) was proposed to address the limitations of existing Gaussian splatting methods in rendering reflective objects with inter-reflection effects.
It builds on the work of 3D Gaussian Splatting (Kerbl et al., 2023) and 2D Gaussian Splatting (Huang et al., 2024).
It differs from GShader (Jiang et al., 2024) by using deferred shading and from RelightableGaussian (Gao et al., 2023) by using ray tracing on an extracted mesh for visibility.
